items.abstract: <jats:p>The complex elliptic Ginibre ensemble with coupling constant τ is a complex Gaussian matrix interpolating between the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble (GUE) and the complex Ginibre ensemble. It has been known for some time that its eigenvalues form a determinantal point process in the complex plane. Until recently, however, Kanazawa and Kieburg [35] have proved that the singular values form a Pfaffian point process. In this paper we consider an extended complex elliptic Ginibre ensemble, which connects the GUE and the spiked complex Wishart ensemble, and investigate local statistics of the singular values. Particularly as τ tends to 1 at a certain critical rate, we prove that the limiting distribution of the largest singular value is described as a new Fredholm Pfaffian series, which connects two distributions FGUE and FGUE2 where FGUE is the GUE Tracy-Widom distribution.</jats:p>
title: Singular value statistics for the spiked elliptic Ginibre ensemble

items.abstract: <jats:p>Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) is known as an effective method for extracting dominant dynamic structures from complex unsteady flow fields. One challenge in applying DMD to engineering problems is that conventional algorithms require substantial computational resources, particularly regarding memory consumption and data storage. On-the-fly DMD algorithms have been proposed to address these limitations. In this study, we further enhance the on-the-fly Total DMD approach by incorporating Incremental Singular Value Decomposition (ISVD). A key advantage of our on-the-fly Total DMD algorithm with ISVD is that it enables both the computation of DMD modes with reduced memory requirements and the subsequent application of Sparsity-Promoting DMD (SPDMD) for dominant mode identification, all without the need to store the entire flow field on disk during CFD simulations. We verify that our algorithm successfully captures the dominant modes, yielding results comparable to those obtained by conventional Total DMD combined with SPDMD</jats:p>
title: On-the-fly algorithm for Dynamic Mode Decomposition using Incremental Singular Value Decomposition and Total Least Squares

items.abstract: <jats:p>Let $F_n$ be an $n$ by $n$ symmetric matrix whose entries are bounded by $n^{\gamma}$ for some $\gamma>0$. Consider a randomly perturbed matrix $M_n=F_n+X_n$, where $X_n$ is a {\it random symmetric matrix} whose upper diagonal entries $x_{ij}, 1\le i\le j,$ are iid copies of a random variable $\xi$. Under a very general assumption on $\xi$, we show that for any $B>0$ there exists $A>0$ such that $\mathbb{P}(\sigma_n(M_n)\le n^{-A})\le n^{-B}$.</jats:p>
title: On the least singular value of random symmetric matrices

items.abstract: <jats:p>Dans cet article, nous considérons des N×N matrices DN, avec des entrées i.i.d. de loi a-stable normalisés par N1/a. Nous démontrons que la plus petite valeur singulière de DN, multipliée par N, tend vers la même loi que dans le cas gaussien, pour presque tout a∈(0,2). Ceci est établi en considérant la symétrisation de la matrice DN et en utilisant une version de la stratégie en trois étapes, une stratégie bien connue en théorie des matrices aléatoires. Pour utiliser cette approche, nous établissons également une loi locale isotrope pour la matrice symétrisée et légèrement perturbée par une matrice gaussienne de structure similaire. Cette loi locale isotrope est établie pour une classe générale de matrices qui satisfont des hypothèses de régularité. Nous démontrons également la délocalisation complète des vecteurs propres à gauche et à droite de DN, associés aux énergies dans un petit intervalle autour de 0.</jats:p>
title: Universality of the least singular value and singular vector delocalisation for Lévy non-symmetric random matrices
